title: Identifying Fairness Issues in Automatically Generated Testing Content

bias_targets.methodology: Annotating generated English proficiency test stimuli for construct-irrelevant knowledge (KSA), such as US-centric cultural references, specific regionalisms, or unfamiliar contexts, and evaluating automated classification models like fine-tuned BERT and GPT-4 with self-correcting prompts to detect these issues.

Annotating generated test stimuli for offensive, controversial, upsetting, or overly negative content that could trigger strong emotions and distract test-takers, and assessing various NLP classification techniques to filter out these issues.

Evaluated as part of the KSA (Knowledge, Skill, and Ability) fairness guidelines by identifying and filtering test content that assumes familiarity with elitist activities, luxury items, or specific financial statuses, using human expert annotation and guided LLM prompting.
